### CVE-2026-6103 — Phar TAR phar_tar_number() Integer Overflow - Archive Entry Injection
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-09-25 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 4.3
- CWE: CWE-190 CWE-190 Integer overflow or wraparound
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 4.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:L/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

phar_tar_number() parses the octal size field of a TAR header into a uint32_t with no overflow check. The field is 11 octal digits wide and holds values up to 0x1FFFFFFFF, so a size above 0xFFFFFFFF silently wraps. The parser then skips the wrong number of data blocks and interprets attacker-controlled file content as the next TAR header, which lets a crafted archive inject entries that PharData reports and extracts as if they were genuine.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.34 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.35 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.26 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.11 (semver)

Credits: @arnoldasr (GitHub); @Oblivionsage (GitHub); @OSTIF-Derek (GitHub); Jakub Zelenka; Weilin Du

### CVE-2026-6104 — Global buffer over-read in mb_convert_encoding() with attacker-supplied encoding
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-05-10 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-125 CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read; CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 6.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:L/SC:L/SI:N/SA:L/RE:M/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:H`

In PHP versions 8.4.* before 8.4.21 and 8.5.* before 8.5.6, when an encoding name containing an embedded NUL byte is passed to mb_convert_encoding() or related mbstring functions, the code incorrectly assumes that when strncasecmp() returns 0 it means the strings have the same length. This can lead to out-of-bounds read of global memory, potentially causing a crash or information disclosure or crash. Affected functions include mb_convert_encoding(), mb_detect_encoding(), mb_convert_variables(), and mb_detect_order(), as well as the mbstring.detect_order and mbstring.http_output INI settings.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.4.* <8.4.21 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-6722 — Use-After-Free in SOAP using Apache map
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-05-10 | Updated: 2026-07-23 | Max CVSS: 9.5
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free; CWE-825 Expired Pointer Dereference
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.5 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H/AU:Y/RE:M/U:Red`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L`

In PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.31, 8.3.* before 8.3.31, 8.4.* before 8.4.21, and 8.5.* before 8.5.6, the SOAP extension's object deduplication mechanism stores pointers to PHP objects in a global map without incrementing their reference counts. When an apache:Map node contains duplicate keys, processing the second entry overwrites the first in the temporary result map, freeing the original PHP object while its stale pointer remains in the map. A subsequent href reference to the freed node can copy the dangling pointer into the result. As PHP string allocations can reclaim the freed memory region, an attacker with control over the SOAP request body can exploit this use-after-free to achieve remote code execution.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.31 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.31 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.21 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-7262 — NULL pointer dereference in SOAP apache:Map decoder with missing <value>
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-05-10 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-476 CWE-476 NULL pointer dereference; CWE-476 NULL Pointer Dereference
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 2.9 LOW `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P/AU:Y/RE:M/U:Amber`

- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

In PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.31, 8.3.* before 8.3.31, 8.4.* before 8.4.21, and 8.5.* before 8.5.6, when a SOAP server has a typemap configured, the decoding process contains a mistake which checks the wrong variable in case of missing value element.  This leads to dereferences a NULL pointer, causing a segmentation fault. This allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to crash the PHP SOAP server process, resulting in denial of service.

In PHP versions 8.4.* before 8.4.21 and 8.5.* before 8.5.6, DOMNode::C14N() method may process the XML data incorrectly, causing a circular linked list in the data structure representing the XML document. This may cause subsequent processing of the XML document to enter infinite loop, causing denial of service in the processing application.

### CVE-2026-7568 — Signed integer overflow in metaphone()
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-05-10 | Updated: 2026-07-15 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-190 CWE-190 Integer Overflow or Wraparound; CWE-125 CWE-125 Out-of-bounds Read; CWE-190 Integer Overflow or Wraparound
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 6.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:L/SI:L/SA:L/RE:L/U:Amber`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial
- CVSS 3.1 (redhat-SADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`

In PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.31, 8.3.* before 8.3.31, 8.4.* before 8.4.21, and 8.5.* before 8.5.6, the metaphone() function in ext/standard/metaphone.c uses a signed int variable to track the current position within the input string. If a string longer than 2,147,483,647 bytes is passed, a signed integer overflow occurs, resulting in undefined behavior. This can lead to an out-of-bounds read, causing a segmentation fault or access to unrelated memory, and may affect the availability of the PHP process.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.31 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.31 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.21 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.6 (semver)

### CVE-2026-24895 — FrankenPHP affected by Path Confusion via Unicode casing in CGI path splitting allows execution of arbitrary files
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-02-12 | Updated: 2026-02-12 | Max CVSS: 8.9
- CWE: CWE-180 CWE-180: Incorrect Behavior Order: Validate Before Canonicalize
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.9 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

FrankenPHP is a modern application server for PHP. Prior to 1.11.2, FrankenPHP’s CGI path splitting logic improperly handles Unicode characters during case conversion. The logic computes the split index (for finding .php) on a lowercased copy of the request path but applies that byte index to the original path. Because strings.ToLower() in Go can increase the byte length of certain UTF-8 characters (e.g., Ⱥ expands when lowercased), the computed index may not align with the correct position in the original string. This results in an incorrect SCRIPT_NAME and SCRIPT_FILENAME, potentially causing FrankenPHP to execute a file other than the one intended by the URI. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.11.2.

Affected:
- php / frankenphp: affected < 1.11.2

References:
- https://github.com/php/frankenphp/security/advisories/GHSA-g966-83w7-6w38 [x_refsource_CONFIRM]

FrankenPHP is a modern application server for PHP. From version 1.11.2 to before version 1.12.3, the splitPos() function in cgi.go misuses golang.org/x/text/search with search.IgnoreCase when the request path contains a non-ASCII byte. - SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

HAX CMS helps manage microsite universe with PHP or NodeJs backends. Prior to version 26.0.0 of HAX CMS PHP, the `saveFile` endpoint validates upload extensions case-insensitively and writes the filename to disk verbatim, but the `.htaccess` rule that forces `Content-Disposition: attachment` on HTML files is case-sensitive. An HTML file uploaded with an uppercase extension (`.HTML`, `.Html`, `.HTM`) is still served as `text/html` but the forced-download header never applies, so the browser renders it inline and executes any embedded JavaScript in the HAXcms origin. This bypasses the mitigation shipped for CVE-2026-22704. Version 26.0.0 contains a fix.

Affected:
- haxtheweb / haxcms-php: affected < 26.0.0

HAX CMS helps manage microsite universe with PHP or NodeJs backends. Prior to version 26.0.0, an OS command injection vulnerability exists in the Git.php library of the HAXcms PHP backend. ### CVE-2026-50275 — Datadog PHP Tracer: Improper parsing of W3C baggage headers may lead to DoS
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-09-17 | Updated: 2026-09-18 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-770 CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

The Datadog PHP Tracer provides application performance monitoring and distributed tracing for PHP. Prior to 1.19.2, ddtrace_deserialize_baggage in ext/distributed_tracing_headers.c parses incoming W3C baggage HTTP headers without enforcing DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_ITEMS or DD_TRACE_BAGGAGE_MAX_BYTES. A remote unauthenticated client can send an arbitrarily large number of comma-separated key-value pairs or a single oversized value, causing the tracer to allocate hash-map entries and consume unbounded CPU and memory on each request. Baggage extraction is enabled by default in most affected deployments unless baggage is removed from DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_STYLE or DD_TRACE_PROPAGATION_STYLE_EXTRACT. This issue is fixed in version 1.19.2.

Affected:
- DataDog / dd-trace-php: affected < 1.19.2

### CVE-2026-54133 — jmespath.php has CompilerRuntime code injection via unescaped function names
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-06-12 | Updated: 2026-06-12 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20: Improper Input Validation; CWE-94 CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection'); CWE-116 CWE-116: Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

jmespath.php allows users to use JMESPath, software for declaratively specifying how to extract elements from a JSON document, in PHP applications with PHP data structures. Versions prior to 2.9.1 can generate and execute attacker-controlled PHP code when `JmesPath\CompilerRuntime` is used with an attacker-controlled JMESPath expression. The compiler emits parsed JMESPath function names into generated PHP source without sufficient escaping. A crafted expression can cause the generated cache file to contain executable attacker-controlled PHP, which is then loaded by the compiler runtime. The issue is patched in `2.9.1` and later. As a workaround, disable `JP_PHP_COMPILE` and do not use `JmesPath\CompilerRuntime` with attacker-controlled expressions. Use the default `AstRuntime` for untrusted expressions. Applications that must continue accepting untrusted JMESPath expressions before upgrading should ensure those expressions are never evaluated by the compiler runtime.

Affected:
- jmespath / jmespath.php: affected < 2.9.1

References:
- https://github.com/jmespath/jmespath.php/security/advisories/GHSA-pcw8-m77r-2528 [x_refsource_CONFIRM]

- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-08-07 | Updated: 2026-08-07 | Max CVSS: 6.9

Smarty is a template engine for PHP, facilitating the separation of presentation (HTML/CSS) from application logic. From 5.0.0 until 5.8.4, Smarty's stream: resource-name handling does not adequately restrict which PHP stream wrappers and filter chains can be referenced from a template, allowing a php://filter-wrapped resource name to be used to read the contents of arbitrary local files accessible to the PHP process. An attacker able to author or influence a template's resource reference could exploit this to disclose sensitive file contents outside the intended template/config scope. This issue is fixed in version 5.8.4.

ALTCHA PHP is a lightweight PHP library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges. From 2.0.0 until 2.0.3, the verifySolution method skips HMAC signature verification when a challenge payload omits the signature field, even when hmacSignatureSecret is configured. An attacker can remove the signature, supply attacker-selected low-difficulty challenge parameters, solve the resulting proof of work, and submit a payload that verifies successfully, bypassing the CAPTCHA control. This issue is fixed in version 2.0.3.

### CVE-2026-82416 — FrankenPHP: Cross-request PHP session ID leak in worker mode when the session extension is a shared module
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-10-13 | Updated: 2026-10-13 | Max CVSS: 7.7
- CWE: CWE-362 CWE-362: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition'); CWE-488 CWE-488: Exposure of Data Element to Wrong Session
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:L`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

FrankenPHP is a modern application server for PHP. Prior to 1.12.5, FrankenPHP worker mode can retain PHP session state between requests when the session extension is loaded as a shared module and is unavailable through HAVE_PHP_SESSION at compile time. In this build configuration, frankenphp_reset_session_state() is compiled out, PS(id) can survive a request boundary, and a subsequent session_start() can ignore the new request's cookie because an identifier is already present. Under concurrent requests, session_id() can therefore return another client's identifier or a stale identifier from a previous request on the same worker thread, causing cross-user session exposure, possible session hijacking, and intermittent logout behavior. Builds with the session extension statically linked, including the official static binaries and Docker images, are not affected. This issue is fixed in version 1.12.5.

Affected:
- php / frankenphp: affected < 1.12.5

References:
- https://github.com/php/frankenphp/security/advisories/GHSA-v3ph-cgqh-r8p5 [x_refsource_CONFIRM]

### CVE-2026-91765 — SOAP: Unbounded Recursion in Server-Side cleanup_xml_node
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-09-25 | Updated: 2026-09-28 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-674 CWE-674
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

cleanup_xml_node() in the SOAP XML parser recurses once per XML nesting level with no depth limit. An unauthenticated attacker can post a SOAP request containing tens of thousands of nested elements to any SoapServer endpoint, exhaust the stack and crash the process. The same unbounded recursion exists in the SOAP value decoder and in the WSDL node search helper.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.34 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.35 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.26 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.11 (semver)

Credits: ExPatch_LLC; Alexandre Daubois

### CVE-2026-93682 — Out-of-bounds read in the HTTP stream wrapper when following a redirect with an empty Location header
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-09-25 | Updated: 2026-09-25 | Max CVSS: 5.8
- CWE: CWE-125 CWE-125 Out-of-bounds read
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 5.8 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

When the HTTP stream wrapper follows a redirect and the response carries a Location header with an empty value, the redirect code reads one byte past the end of the heap buffer holding the location. The value of that out-of-bounds byte decides which redirect target is built, so a malicious server controls whether the client is sent to the host root or to the current directory.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.34 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.35 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.26 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.11 (semver)

Credits: Ilia Alshanetsky; Jordi Kroon; David Carlier; Xinchen Hui

### CVE-2026-107376 — webonyx graphql-php: Unbounded recursion in parser causes stack overflow on crafted nested input
- Assigner: GitHub_M | Published: 2026-10-08 | Updated: 2026-10-08 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-674 CWE-674: Uncontrolled Recursion
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

webonyx graphql-php is a PHP implementation of the GraphQL specification. Prior to 15.32.3, GraphQL\Language\Parser performs recursive descent without a recursion limit in parseSelectionSet, parseValueLiteral, and parseTypeReference. A remote attacker can submit deeply nested selection sets, object or list values, or list types that exhaust the PHP process stack during pre-validation parsing, before query validation and complexity controls run. The resulting SIGSEGV can terminate PHP-FPM workers or long-running Swoole, RoadRunner, ReactPHP, or CLI processes and cannot be caught by application-level exception handling. This issue is fixed in version 15.32.3.

Affected:
- webonyx / graphql-php: affected < 15.32.3

### CVE-2026-109618 — RCE via OOM corruption
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-11-24 | Max CVSS: 9.8
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use after free; CWE-755 CWE-755 Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions; CWE-824 CWE-824 Access of uninitialized pointer; CWE-1325 CWE-1325 Improperly controlled sequential memory allocation; CWE-1419 CWE-1419 Incorrect Initialization of Resource
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 4.0 (nvd:security@php.net:Secondary): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:X/CR:X/IR:X/AR:X/MAV:X/MAC:X/MAT:X/MPR:X/MUI:X/MVC:X/MVI:X/MVA:X/MSC:X/MSI:X/MSA:X/S:X/AU:X/R:X/V:X/RE:X/U:X`
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:nvd@nist.gov:Primary): 9.8 CRITICAL `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- **CISA KEV**: added 2026-10-26, ransomware=Unknown — PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability
- Exploit-DB 52704: PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618) - PHP core versions after v5.4 - RCE (remote/php, 2026-10-22, verified=1)

PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

**workarounds:** Check the GitHub Security Advisory for mitigation strategies.

### CVE-2026-109619 — RCE via stale global state
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-10-21 | Updated: 2026-11-24 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use after free; CWE-755 CWE-755 Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions; CWE-824 CWE-824 Access of uninitialized pointer; CWE-1325 CWE-1325 Improperly controlled sequential memory allocation; CWE-1419 CWE-1419 Incorrect Initialization of Resource
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=active, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total
- CVSS 4.0 (nvd:security@php.net:Secondary): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:X/CR:X/IR:X/AR:X/MAV:X/MAC:X/MAT:X/MPR:X/MUI:X/MVC:X/MVI:X/MVA:X/MSC:X/MSI:X/MSA:X/S:X/AU:X/R:X/V:X/RE:X/U:X`
- CVSS 3.1 (nvd:nvd@nist.gov:Primary): 8.1 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- **CISA KEV**: added 2026-10-26, ransomware=Unknown — PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability

PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

**workarounds:** Check the GitHub Security Advisory for mitigation strategies.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.2.* <8.2.35 (semver); affected 8.3.* <8.3.36 (semver); affected 8.4.* <8.4.27 (semver); affected 8.5.* <8.5.12 (semver)

### CVE-2026-114422 — Enable Media Replace 4.1.4 - 4.2.2 - Unauthenticated PHP Object Injection via Metadata Replacer
- Assigner: WPScan | Published: 2026-10-30 | Updated: 2026-10-30 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data; CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The Enable Media Replace WordPress plugin before 4.2.3 does not restrict the classes allowed when deserializing stored metadata during its media replace-and-update-links routine, allowing unauthenticated users to inject a PHP object that is instantiated when a user with upload access performs a routine media replacement, resulting in PHP Object Injection and local file inclusion of existing PHP/HTML files, which can be escalated to remote code execution where an attacker-influenced PHP or HTML file is present on the server.
This is a regression of CVE-2023-4643, which was fixed in 4.1.3 and reintroduced in 4.1.4.

Affected:
- Unknown / Enable Media Replace: affected 4.1.4 <4.2.3 (semver)

Credits: Jakub Herman; WPScan

### CVE-2026-115560 — Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-20 CWE-20 Improper Input Validation; CWE-502 CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.

Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 0 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

Credits: Dvir Sasson (ZEST Security); Frédéric Le Roch; Carlos Perez (Lazarus Technology); HarukaKaya; nvr0x5; Katika Mohaseen; Jackson Tai; Crain; Ilija Tovilo; Arnaud Le Blanc

### CVE-2026-118064 — Advance Guest Post <= 1.9 - Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload via featured_action
- Assigner: WPScan | Published: 2026-11-13 | Updated: 2026-11-13 | Max CVSS: 9.8

The Advance Guest Post WordPress plugin through 1.9 does not properly restrict or validate file uploads, authorizing an upload action with a nonce exposed to every front-end visitor and checking only a file's leading bytes, allowing unauthenticated users to upload arbitrary PHP files and execute code remotely.

Successful exploitation additionally requires the target to run PHP 7.x; on PHP 8.0 and later the vulnerable code path raises a fatal error before the file is written.

### CVE-2026-126714 — Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-367 CWE-367 Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition; CWE-662 CWE-662 Improper Synchronization
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 0 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

Credits: Leo Lin; Asahi; Ilija Tovilo; Arnaud Le Blanc

### CVE-2026-127960 — Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-19 | Max CVSS: 8.7
- CWE: CWE-400 CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption; CWE-407 CWE-407 Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.1.32 <=8.1.34 (semver); affected 8.2.28 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.18 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.5 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

Credits: benzdeus; Stephan Lipp (Ada Logics / Anthropic); Jakub Zelenka; Arnaud Le Blanc

### CVE-2026-128064 — Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-19 | Max CVSS: 8.2
- CWE: CWE-319 CWE-319 Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.2 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 0 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

### CVE-2026-128090 — PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-20 | Max CVSS: 7.7
- CWE: CWE-347 CWE-347 Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature; CWE-757 CWE-757 Selection of Less-Secure Algorithm During Negotiation
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 0 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

### CVE-2026-129182 — Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-24 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free; CWE-459 CWE-459 Incomplete Cleanup
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown.

A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

Credits: Alexandre Daubois; n132; Go Kudo; Arnaud Le Blanc; Jakub Zelenka; Ilija Tovilo

References:
- https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-2fjv-p558-g82m [vendor-advisory]

### CVE-2026-129289 — PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-22 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-444 CWE-444 Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests; CWE-670 CWE-670 Always-Incorrect Control Flow Implementation
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=total

PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 0 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

### CVE-2026-129291 — PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-20 | Max CVSS: 8.8
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 8.8 HIGH `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.1.20 <=8.1.34 (semver); affected 8.2.7 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

Credits: Thomas Chauchefoin; Ian P. Christian; Nora Dossche; Jakub Zelenka

References:

### CVE-2026-129474 — Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution

Use-after-free in magic method backtraces can lead to remote code execution.

When collecting the arguments of a method call handled by __call() or __callStatic() for a backtrace, PHP can read stale values that may refer to freed memory. If a fatal error such as exceeding memory_limit occurs while an application enters such a call, with fatal_error_backtraces enabled (the default) and zend.exception_ignore_args disabled, a remote attacker who controls enough request data to influence memory allocation may cause memory corruption, crash the PHP worker or, with knowledge of memory addresses, execute arbitrary code. php.ini-production enables zend.exception_ignore_args, which prevents this.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

### CVE-2026-129481 — Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-19 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free; CWE-459 CWE-459 Incomplete Cleanup
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Use-after-free after interrupted session shutdown.

The session extension records the filename of the executing script when a session starts. If a fatal error occurs in an application callback while the session variables are destroyed at shutdown, such as stream_close() of a user-defined stream wrapper, the pointer is retained after the request memory is freed, and a later request handled by the same worker can free the stale string. An attacker who can trigger such a failing cleanup may crash the worker or corrupt memory; code execution has not been demonstrated. This requires the filename to be allocated in request memory, for example when the script is not cached by OPcache.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)

### CVE-2026-129496 — Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution
- Assigner: php | Published: 2026-11-19 | Updated: 2026-11-20 | Max CVSS: 9.2
- CWE: CWE-416 CWE-416 Use After Free; CWE-459 CWE-459 Incomplete Cleanup
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 9.2 CRITICAL `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution.

In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. A diagnostic raised early in the first request of a worker, such as the max_input_vars warning, then accesses the freed cache. On such a deployment an unauthenticated remote attacker can crash PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php or CGI workers with a crafted request. Arbitrary code execution may be possible and has been demonstrated with known memory addresses.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Affected:
- PHP Group / PHP: affected 0 <8.2.36 (semver); affected 8.3.0 <8.3.37 (semver); affected 8.4.0 <8.4.28 (semver); affected 8.5.0 <8.5.13 (semver)
